messages.subject: Missing value in response
parts: Hi, everyone. I have one quesition about missing value in response or outcome. Right now my real data (response) has some missing values, and I directly use it to a cognitive diagnosis model. But I always have: logProb is -Inf. I am wondeing if there is any trick about this? Could I just use NA in the outcome? THanks!

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Missing value in response
parts:
Duoduo, thanks for your question.  Missing (NA) values in the response will generally be handled fine.  One exception is if you have a partially-observed response vector following a multivariate distribution (for example, a multivariate normal likelihood distribution, where only some elements of the response vector are observed and some are NA), in which case special care might be necessary.  But, if your response data are scalar observations (each following a univariate distribution), then the MCMC will handle these missing (NA) values with posterior predictive samplers.

If you want to avoid issues of logProb being -Inf, you can try providing values for the missing observations using the initial values list when building the model.

If one of your MCMC samplers is repeatedly issuing warnings about logProbs being -Inf, on every MCMC iteration, then something might be going wrong.

Cheers,
Daniel
